context: Removes the eviction logic from the in-memory response cache since 'it was rarely hitting the limit anyway'.
explanation: Without MAX_ENTRIES and the eviction check, cache is a Map that only ever grows for the lifetime of the process. Every distinct key (e.g. per query string, per user) adds an entry that's never removed, which is a textbook unbounded-growth memory leak that will eventually exhaust the process's memory under real traffic. Fix: keep a bounded eviction policy (LRU/size cap) or move the cache to something with built-in TTL/size limits (e.g. lru-cache, Redis).
